gianlucabocanegra/iphs400-mp2-cms#5\nnumber:\t4\n--\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nAn Editor can publish a Draft Post and unpublish a Published one. Confirmation screens come in T05. When the developer runs an Export (`cms publish` then `cms deploy`), only Published Posts are written to `site/`, and the public site goes live on GitHub Pages. The Home page shows the latest 5 News, `noticias/` lists all News, and every Published Post gets its own page. The site is in Spanish, dates are in Lima time, and no Author names appear. Markdown is sanitized and every link and asset path is relative. Each Export is recorded.\n\nThis completes the first end-to-end path: login → write → publish → Export → live site.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Editor can publish a Draft Post and unpublish a Published one. Unpublishing returns the Post to Draft.\n- [ ] Publishing sets the first-published time, which never changes afterwards. The Slug can't be edited once a Post has been published, even after Unpublishing.\n- [ ] `render_site(out, export_date=...)` writes only Published Posts; a Draft never appears as a page, feed entry or Home page item.\n- [ ] The Home page shows the latest 5 Published News, newest first; `noticias/index.html` lists all Published News.\n- [ ] Each Published Post has its own page under its kind's folder.\n- [ ] News dates show the first-published date in Spanish, in America/Lima (\"29 de septiembre de 2026\").\n- [ ] No Author name appears anywhere in `site/`.\n- [ ] A `<script>` in a body is stripped in `site/`.\n- [ ] No `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` appears in any file under `site/`.\n- [ ] Each Export records the time it ran.\n- [ ] The site is deployed with `cms deploy`, the GitHub Pages URL loads with the stylesheet, and the URL is recorded in the README.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #3 (T02)\n------SPEC\ntitle:\tSpec: Golf & Country Club of Trujillo CMS\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tgianlucabocanegra\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, spec\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t1\n--\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe Golf & Country Club of Trujillo announces news, events and the weekly restaurant menu through WhatsApp groups and Instagram. Messages get buried, they're hard to search, and there's no single place that's always up to date. Members keep asking the office the same questions.\n\nThe office wants to post an update in a few minutes without asking anyone for help. The club has three fears:\n- a staff member publishes an unfinished post, or a wrong menu or price, by mistake;\n- someone who should only post news changes the rules or membership Pages, or adds or removes Users;\n- a Draft shows up on the public site.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with two halves, following ADR-001 and ADR-002.\n\n- **Admin console** (English, local only). Editors write and publish Posts of three kinds: News, Event and Menu. Admins also manage Pages (rules, membership, about) and Users. Every change Members will see needs an explicit Confirmation, with a preview.\n- **Public site** (Spanish, static). Each Export renders Published content into `site/`, and it is deployed to GitHub Pages. The generated Home page shows the Current menu, Upcoming Events and the latest News. Navigation adds three fixed feeds (News, Events, Menu archive) and the Admin's Pages in the order the Admin sets.\n\nThe developer runs the Export, never the office. The console shows how many changes are not yet Live, so nobody confuses Published with Live.\n\nVocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md` throughout.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Login and session\n\n1. As a User, I want to sign in with my email and password, so that only club staff can reach the console.\n2. As a User, I want a wrong email or password to give the same generic error, so that nobody can find out which emails have accounts.\n3. As a User, I want to sign out, so that the next person at the office computer isn't working as me.\n4. As a Deactivated User, I want my login to be refused, so that former staff can't change the site.\n5. As an Admin, I want a User I deactivate to lose access on their very next request, even if they're already signed in, so that deactivation takes effect immediately.\n6. As a visitor who isn't signed in, I want every console address to send me to the login screen, so that no console content leaks.\n7. As the club, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes and never logged, so that a copied database doesn't reveal them.\n8. As the club, I want every form that changes something to carry a CSRF token, so that another website can't make a signed-in User's browser change content.\n\n### Roles\n\n9. As an Editor, I want the console to show me only Posts, the dashboard and signing out, so that I'm not distracted by things I can't use.\n10. As the club, I want an Editor who types a Page or User address directly to be refused with a \"not allowed\" response, so that the restriction is real and not just a hidden link.\n11. As an Admin, I want to do everything an Editor can, plus manage Pages and Users, so that one person can run the whole site.\n\n### Posts\n\n12. As an Editor, I want to create a Post by choosing its kind (News, Event or Menu), so that it appears in the right place on the public site.\n13. As an Editor, I want to write a Post body in Markdown, so that I can add headings, lists and links without a complicated editor.\n14. As an Editor, I want a new Post to start as a Draft, so that nothing reaches Members until I decide.\n15. As an Editor, I want the Slug generated from the title with accents stripped (\"Menú de la semana\" → `menu-de-la-semana`), so that I never have to think about addresses.\n16. As an Editor, I want to edit the Slug before first publish, so that I can shorten an awkward one.\n17. As a Member, I want a Slug to never change once content has been Published, even after it's Unpublished and republished, so that links shared on WhatsApp keep working.\n18. As an Editor, I want a clash with an existing Slug to be fixed automatically by adding a number (`-2`, `-3`), so that I can reuse a common title such as \"Menú de la semana\" every week.\n19. As an Editor, I want a clear error if I type a Slug that's already taken, so that I don't overwrite someone else's address.\n20. As an Editor, I want to preview a Post as Members will see it (Spanish public layout, sanitized Markdown), so that I catch mistakes before they go Live.\n21. As an Editor, I want to edit, publish, unpublish or delete any Post, including one written by another Editor, so that whoever is in the office can fix Friday's menu on Monday.\n22. As the club, I want the Author to stay the original writer when someone else edits a Post, so that the console records who created it.\n23. As an Admin, I want to do anything to Posts that an Editor can, so that I can cover for the office.\n\n### Events\n\n24. As an Editor, I want to give an Event a start date, an optional start time and an optional end date, so that a dinner at 8 pm and a Saturday–Sunday tournament are both described precisely.\n25. As an Editor, I want an Event without a start date to be rejected, so that every Event can be sorted.\n26. As an Editor, I want an end date earlier than the start date to be rejected with a clear message, so that impossible ranges never go Live.\n27. As a Member, I want the Event date shown first and prominently on every Event, so that I can tell at a glance when it is.\n28. As a Member, I want Upcoming Events listed soonest first, so that \"when is the next event?\" is answered at the top.\n29. As a Member, I want a weekend tournament to stay Upcoming until its end date has passed, so that I can still find it while it's happening.\n\n### Menu\n\n30. As an Editor, I want to post each week's menu as a new Menu Post, so that updating it takes a few minutes.\n31. As a Member, I want the Home page to show only the Current menu, so that I never read last week's prices by mistake.\n32. As a Member, I want older Menus in a Menu archive, so that I can look up what was served before.\n33. As an Editor, I want the previous Menu to leave the Home page automatically when the new one goes Live, so that nobody has to remember to unpublish it.\n\n### Confirmation\n\n34. As an Editor, I want publishing to go through a Confirmation screen showing the preview, so that an unfinished post or a wrong price isn't published by one careless click.\n35. As an Editor, I want saving edits to Published content to go through the same Confirmation, so that a price change to a Live menu is checked before it goes out.\n36. As an Editor, I want unpublishing to need Confirmation, so that I don't accidentally take down something Members rely on.\n37. As an Editor, I want deleting to need Confirmation that says it's permanent, so that I don't lose content by mistake.\n38. As an Editor, I want to cancel on the Confirmation screen and return to my unsaved edits, so that I can fix the mistake I just noticed.\n39. As an Editor, I want saving a Draft to need no Confirmation, so that everyday writing stays quick.\n\n### Pages\n\n40. As an Admin, I want to create, edit, preview, publish, unpublish and delete Pages (rules, membership, about) with the same Draft/Published lifecycle and Confirmation as Posts, so that I only learn one workflow.\n41. As an Admin, I want to give each Page a navigation order number, so that Members see the Pages in a sensible order.\n42. As a Member, I want every Live Page to appear in the Navigation, so that I can find the rules and membership information.\n43. As the club, I want a Page Slug that clashes with a public-site address (`index`, `noticias`, `eventos`, `menus`, `style`) to be rejected, so that a Page can never overwrite the Home page or a feed.\n\n### Users\n\n44. As an Admin, I want to create a User with a name, email, role and initial password, so that new office staff can start posting.\n45. As an Admin, I want to change a User's role between Admin and Editor, so that responsibilities can change.\n46. As an Admin, I want to deactivate and reactivate a User, so that former staff lose access without their content or authorship being lost.\n47. As an Admin, I want to be prevented from deactivating or demoting myself, so that the club always has an Admin.\n48. As an Admin, I want to see all Users with their role and whether they're active, so that I know who has access.\n49. As the club, I want Users never to be deleted, so that every Post and Page keeps its Author.\n\n### Dashboard and content lists\n\n50. As a User, I want a dashboard with counts of Posts by kind and status, and (for Admins) Pages by status, so that I can see the state of the site at a glance.\n51. As a User, I want the dashboard to show how many changes are not yet Live and when the last Export happened, so that I know when to ask for an Export.\n52. As a User, I want to filter the Post list by kind and by status, so that I can find this week's Draft menu quickly.\n53. As a User, I want the Post list to show title, kind, status, Author and last-updated time in Lima time, so that I can tell what changed recently.\n54. As a User, I want status filters that match no content to still appear, showing zero, so that the list doesn't change shape the way WordPress's did.\n\n### Public site\n\n55. As a Member, I want a Home page with the Current menu, the next Upcoming Events and the latest News, so that I can find what I need in a few seconds.\n56. As a Member, I want News, Events and Menu archive feeds in the Navigation, so that I can browse each kind of Post.\n57. As a Member, I want the Events feed to show Upcoming Events first and then past Events, most recent first, so that the list stays useful after an event is over.\n58. As a Member, I want the public site entirely in Spanish, dates included (\"29 de septiembre de 2026\"), so that it reads naturally.\n59. As a Member, I want every date and time shown in Lima time, so that a post never appears dated tomorrow.\n60. As a Member, I want News and Menus dated by when they were first published, so that the date means \"when the club said this\".\n61. As the club, I want no Author names on the public site, so that the club speaks as one voice.\n62. As the club, I want Drafts never to appear on the public site in any form (page, feed entry, Home page or Navigation), so that the club's third fear can't happen.\n63. As the club, I want user-written Markdown sanitized before it's rendered, so that a pasted `<script>` can't run in a Member's browser.\n64. As an Editor, I want to embed an image hosted elsewhere (for example on the club's Instagram) through a Markdown image link, so that posts can have pictures without uploads.\n65. As a Member, I want the site to work from its GitHub Pages subfolder, so that every link and stylesheet loads.\n\n### Export\n\n66. As the developer, I want an Export to render only Published content into `site/` and deploy it, so that what Members see is exactly what is Published.\n67. As the developer, I want each Export to decide Upcoming from the export date in Lima time, so that the result is predictable.\n68. As the developer, I want each Export to record when it ran, so that the console can count changes that aren't Live yet.\n69. As a grader, I want the seed script to create an Admin, an Editor and demo content (at least one Draft and one Published item of each kind, including a multi-day Event), so that the CMS can be tried right away from a fresh clone.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Modules\n\n- **Accounts:** Users, argon2 hashing, login and logout, the signed session cookie, and the rule that a Deactivated User is refused both at login and on every request.\n- **Permissions:** the role check shared by all console routes. Editor: Posts and the dashboard. Admin: everything. It's enforced server-side, and a refusal returns 403.\n- **CSRF:** a per-session token, a hidden field in every state-changing form, and a check on every non-GET console request.\n- **Content:** Posts and Pages, their Draft/Published lifecycle, Slug generation, clash handling and locking, Event-date validation, and the queries for Current menu, Upcoming and the feeds. The console and the Export share it, so both use the same definitions.\n- **Markdown rendering:** one function, used by both Preview and Export, that turns Markdown into sanitized HTML (markdown-it, then nh3). It allows `img` only with an `http(s)` source.\n- **Console routes and templates:** login, dashboard, Post list and editor, Page list and editor, Users, and Confirmation screens. The console is in English.\n- **Export:** `render_site` reads the database and writes the Spanish public site. The `cms publish` and `cms deploy` commands together make up an Export.\n- **Time:** helpers for UTC storage, America/Lima display (standard-library `zoneinfo`) and Spanish date formatting from a hard-coded month list. No new dependency.\n\n### Schema (SQLite; no ORM, following ADR-002's stack)\n\n- **users:** id, name, email (unique, case-insensitive), password_hash, role (`admin` | `editor`), active, created_at.\n- **posts:** id, kind (`news` | `event` | `menu`, fixed at creation), title, slug, body_md, status (`draft` | `published`), author_id, created_at, updated_at, first_published_at, and for Events only: event_start_date, event_start_time (nullable), event_end_date (nullable). The slug is unique within a kind.\n- **pages:** id, title, slug (unique), body_md, status, nav_order, author_id, created_at, updated_at, first_published_at.\n- **exports:** the time each Export ran, plus a count of Published items deleted since then, used by the not-yet-Live indicator.\n- All timestamps are stored in UTC.\n\n### Rules\n\n- **Slug:** generated from the title, lower-case ASCII with accents stripped and hyphens between words. An auto-generated clash gets a numeric suffix; a slug typed by hand that clashes is a form error. The slug can be edited only while `first_published_at` is empty, and once set, that field is never cleared, even by Unpublishing.\n- **Reserved Page Slugs:** `index`, `noticias`, `eventos`, `menus`, `style`.\n- **Event date:** a start date is required. The end date must be on or after the start date. Event fields are rejected on News and Menu Posts.\n- **Upcoming:** `coalesce(event_end_date, event_start_date) >= export_date`, where the export date is a date in America/Lima. The Home page shows the next 3 Upcoming Events.\n- **Current menu:** the Published Menu with the latest `first_published_at`. Every other Published Menu goes to the Menu archive, newest first.\n- **Home page:** the Current menu, the next 3 Upcoming Events and the latest 5 News, all on one page.\n- **Confirmation (no JavaScript):** submitting a change that Members will see (publish, unpublish, delete, or saving Published content) returns a Confirmation page. That page shows a summary and, where relevant, the rendered preview, and carries the pending values in hidden fields with the CSRF token. Only a second POST that includes the confirm flag applies the change. Cancel returns to the editor with the values intact. Saving a Draft applies immediately.\n- **Self-protection:** a request that would deactivate the Admin making it, or change that Admin's own role, is refused with an explanation.\n- **Not-yet-Live indicator:** Posts and Pages whose `updated_at` is after the last Export, plus Published items deleted since then. If there has never been an Export, every Published item counts.\n- **First Admin:** the seed script creates the first Admin and Editor, taking their passwords from `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`. No separate bootstrap command.\n\n### Public site layout (all links relative)\n\n- `index.html`: the Home page.\n- `noticias/index.html` and `noticias/<slug>.html`: News.\n- `eventos/index.html` and `eventos/<slug>.html`: Events (Upcoming, then past).\n- `menus/index.html` and `menus/<slug>.html`: the Menu archive and each Menu.\n- `<slug>.html`: Pages.\n- `style.css`.\n- Navigation order: Inicio, Noticias, Eventos, Menús anteriores, then Pages by nav_order (ties broken by title).\n- The site title comes from `CMS_SITE_TITLE`, set to the club's name in `.env.example`.\n\n### Interfaces that change\n\n- `create_app()` accepts a database path (default from settings), so tests can give each app its own database.\n- `render_site(out, export_date=None)` reads Published content from the configured database. `export_date` defaults to today in America/Lima and records the Export.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **A good test** exercises behaviour through a public seam and asserts only what a User or Member could observe: status codes, redirects, rendered console HTML, and the files and HTML written to `site/`. Tests never query tables or call internal helpers. That lets the storage and module layout change without rewriting tests.\n- **Seam 1, the console over HTTP:** `create_app()` driven by the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. This covers login and deactivation, Permissions (Editor gets 403 on Pages and Users), CSRF rejection, the Post and Page lifecycle, Slug rules, Event-date validation, Confirmation (the first POST changes nothing; the confirmed POST applies), User management and self-protection, the dashboard counts and filters.\n- **Seam 2, Export:** `render_site(tmp_path, export_date=...)`, asserting on the output files. This covers Drafts never being written, the Current menu versus the Menu archive, the Upcoming boundary (the weekend tournament on its last day, and the day after), Navigation order, Spanish dates in Lima time, no Author names, sanitized Markdown (a `<script>` is stripped and an external image survives), and relative paths only.\n- **Fixture change:** each test gets a fresh temporary database seeded with the `DEMO_USERS` admin and editor from the conftest file, so `client_as` works and tests never share state.\n- **Prior art:** `tests/test_t00.py`, which checks the admin page answers over HTTP, that `render_site` writes files, and that paths are relative. `tests/conftest.py` provides the `client_as` pattern. The T00 tests must keep passing.\n- No tests below these two seams.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Media uploads. Images are only Markdown links to files hosted elsewhere.\n- Review or approval workflows, and any status beyond Draft and Published.\n- Scheduled publishing.\n- The office running Exports; there's no Export button in the console.\n- JavaScript on the public site, including client-side Upcoming filtering.\n- Member logins, comments and search.\n- Self-service password change and password reset.\n- Deleting Users.\n- Changing a Post's kind after creation.\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders and WYSIWYG editors (excluded by the assignment).\n- A Spanish admin console.\n- Deploying the admin console anywhere public (ADR-001).\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- The CLI keeps the assignment's command names. In the glossary, running `cms publish` and then `cms deploy` is one Export. The word \"publish\" in the console only ever means the Draft → Published status change.\n- A stale Upcoming list between Exports is accepted: the fix is to Export often, not to add JavaScript.\n- Confirmation is the club's main defence against a wrong price. It applies to Published content edits as well as status changes, because a Live Menu is most often corrected by editing it.\n- Every console route must require login. The permission check applies to routes, not to navigation links.\n\n------\n# Golf & Country Club of Trujillo CMS\n\nA small CMS where the club's office staff write news, events and the weekly menu, and members read them on a public site. The console is in English; the public site is in Spanish, so each term below lists its Spanish label.\n\n## People\n\n**Admin** (Administrador):\nA staff member who manages Pages and Users, and can do everything an Editor can.\n_Avoid_: superuser, owner\n\n**Editor** (Editor):\nA staff member who writes, publishes and fixes any Post, and nothing else. An Editor can never touch Pages or Users.\n_Avoid_: author (as a role), staff, poster\n\n**Author** (Autor):\nThe User who originally wrote a Post or Page. Stays the original writer even when someone else edits it. Visible only in the console, never to Members. An attribute of content, not a role.\n\n**User** (Usuario):\nA login belonging to one staff member, with exactly one role: Admin or Editor. Users are never deleted, only Deactivated.\n_Avoid_: account, member (members are readers, not Users)\n\n**Deactivated** (Desactivado):\nA User who can no longer log in. Their content and authorship stay untouched. An Admin can't deactivate or demote themselves, so the club always has an Admin.\n_Avoid_: deleted, removed, banned\n\n**Member** (Socio):\nA club member or family member who reads the public site. Members never log in.\n_Avoid_: user, reader\n\n## Content\n\n**Post** (Publicación):\nDated content that appears in a feed, not as its own navigation entry. Every Post is exactly one kind: News, Event or Menu.\n_Avoid_: article, entry\n\n**News** (Noticia):\nA Post announcing club news.\n\n**Event** (Evento):\nA Post about something happening at the club, with an Event date.\n\n**Event date** (Fecha del evento):\nWhen an Event happens: a start date, an optional start time and an optional end date for multi-day events such as weekend tournaments. Distinct from when the Post was written or published.\n\n**Upcoming** (Próximos eventos):\nAn Event whose end date (or start date, if there's no end date) is on or after the day of the last Export. A weekend tournament stays Upcoming while it is happening. Decided at Export, not when a Member visits.\n_Avoid_: future, current\n\n**Menu** (Menú de la semana):\nA Post holding the restaurant's menu and prices for one week.\n_Avoid_: menu page\n\n**Current menu** (Menú actual):\nThe newest Live Menu. It's the only Menu shown on the Home page.\n\n**Menu archive** (Menús anteriores):\nThe public list of every Live Menu other than the Current menu.\n\n**Page** (Página):\nStanding content with its own navigation entry, such as rules, membership or about. Only Admins manage Pages, and they set the navigation order.\n_Avoid_: static page\n\n**Home page** (Inicio):\nThe generated public front page showing the Current menu, Upcoming Events and the latest News. Not a Page; nobody writes it.\n_Avoid_: landing page, index page\n\n**Navigation** (Navegación):\nThe public site's top links: Home page first, then the three fixed entries (News, Events, Menu archive), then Pages in Admin-set order.\n_Avoid_: menu (reserved for the restaurant Menu)\n\n**Slug**:\nThe last part of a piece of content's public address, made from its title with accents stripped. Can be edited only before first publish. Never contains a date.\n_Avoid_: permalink, URL\n\n## Publishing\n\n**Draft** (Borrador):\nContent that exists only in the console. A Draft never reaches the public site.\n\n**Published** (Publicado):\nA status only: content marked as belonging on the public site. Becomes Live at the next Export.\n_Avoid_: live (when you mean the status)\n\n**Confirmation** (Confirmación):\nThe explicit second step required before any change to what Members will see: publishing, unpublishing, deleting, or saving edits to Published content.\n_Avoid_: approval, review\n\n**Unpublish** (Despublicar):\nReturning Published content to Draft, so it disappears from the public site at the next Export.\n_Avoid_: hide, archive\n\n**Export** (Exportación):\nRendering all Published content into the public site and deploying it. Run by the developer, never by the office.\n_Avoid_: publish, deploy, build\n\n**Live** (En línea):\nContent that is on the public site right now, because it was Published at the last Export.\n_Avoid_: published (when you mean visible to {"parentUuid":"d2cac2b0-1f80-420b-89ec-e79fe9f403fc","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b6058071-b2f7-48ff-aca8-876b8e74fe25","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01H5pSsBrp21YBBfbMzXCDft","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:create_app\", factory=True, port=args.port,\n                    reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n            return 1\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\n             str(settings.SITE)],\n        )\n        if result.returncode == 0:\n            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n        return result.returncode\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nTwo rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import content, db, settings\nfrom app.markdown import render_markdown\nfrom app.timeutil import fecha, today_lima, utc_now\n\nFOLDERS = {\"news\": \"noticias\", \"event\": \"eventos\", \"menu\": \"menus\"}\nKIND_LABELS_ES = {\"news\": \"Noticia\", \"event\": \"Evento\", \"menu\": \"Menú de la semana\"}\nHOME_NEWS = 5\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef _write(out: Path, name: str, html: str) -> None:\n    path = out / name\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    path.write_text(html)\n\n\ndef _link(post, root: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"A feed entry. `root` is the relative path from the page back to site/.\"\"\"\n    kind = post[\"kind\"]\n    return {\"title\": post[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"{root}{FOLDERS[kind]}/{post['slug']}.html\",\n            \"date\": fecha(post[\"first_published_at\"]) if kind == \"news\" else \"\"}\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None, export_date: date | None = None) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write every Published Post into `out` and record the Export.\n\n    `export_date` (a Lima date) is what Upcoming is measured against from T04 on.\n    \"\"\"\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    export_date = export_date or today_lima()\n    env = environment()\n    db.init_db(settings.DATABASE_PATH)  # an older database may lack `exports`\n    conn = db.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    try:\n        posts = content.published_posts(conn)\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n\n    def page(template: str, depth: int, **ctx) -> str:\n        root = \"../\" * depth\n        nav = [(\"Inicio\", f\"{root}index.html\"), (\"Noticias\", f\"{root}noticias/index.html\")]\n        return env.get_template(template).render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, lang=\"es\", nav=nav, css_path=f\"{root}style.css\",\n            home_path=f\"{root}index.html\", **ctx)\n\n    news = [p for p in posts if p[\"kind\"] == \"news\"]\n    _write(out, \"index.html\", page(\n        \"public/home.html\", 0,\n        news=[_link(p, \"\") for p in news[:HOME_NEWS]]))\n    _write(out, \"noticias/index.html\", page(\n        \"public/feed.html\", 1, page_title=\"Noticias\", heading=\"Noticias\",\n        items=[_link(p, \"../\") for p in news]))\n    for p in posts:\n        _write(out, f\"{FOLDERS[p['kind']]}/{p['slug']}.html\", page(\n            \"public/post.html\", 1, page_title=p[\"title\"], post=p,\n            kind_label=KIND_LABELS_ES[p[\"kind\"]],\n            date_label=fecha(p[\"first_published_at\"]) if p[\"kind\"] == \"news\" else \"\",\n            body_html=render_markdown(p[\"body_md\"])))\n\n    conn = db.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\"INSERT INTO exports (ran_at) VALUES (?)\", (utc_now(),))\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n    return out\n\"\"\"Posts: creation, editing, Slugs and the list. Shared by the console and Export.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nimport unicodedata\n\nfrom app.timeutil import utc_now\n\nKINDS = (\"news\", \"event\", \"menu\")\n\n\nclass PostError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"A problem with what the User typed, worded for the form.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef slugify(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Lower-case ASCII, accents stripped, hyphens between words.\"\"\"\n    plain = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKD\", text).encode(\"ascii\", \"ignore\").decode()\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", plain.lower()).strip(\"-\")\n\n\ndef _taken(conn: sqlite3.Connection, kind: str, slug: str,\n           except_id: int | None) -> bool:\n    return conn.execute(\"SELECT 1 FROM posts WHERE kind = ? AND slug = ? AND id IS NOT ?\",\n                        (kind, slug, except_id)).fetchone() is not None\n\n\ndef _slug_for(conn: sqlite3.Connection, kind: str, title: str, typed: str,\n              except_id: int | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A typed Slug must be free; a generated one gets -2, -3, ... until it is.\"\"\"\n    if typed.strip():\n        slug = slugify(typed)\n        if not slug:\n            raise PostError(\"The slug needs letters or numbers.\")\n        if _taken(conn, kind, slug, except_id):\n            raise PostError(f\"The slug “{slug}” is already used by another post of this kind.\")\n        return slug\n    base = slugify(title)\n    if not base:\n        raise PostError(\"The title needs letters or numbers to make a slug from.\")\n    slug, n = base, 1\n    while _taken(conn, kind, slug, except_id):\n        n += 1\n        slug = f\"{base}-{n}\"\n    return slug\n\n\ndef _clean_title(title: str) -> str:\n    title = title.strip()\n    if not title:\n        raise PostError(\"The title is required.\")\n    return title\n\n\ndef create_post(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, kind: str, title: str, slug: str,\n                body_md: str, author_id: int) -> int:\n    if kind not in KINDS:\n        raise PostError(\"Choose News, Event or Menu.\")\n    title = _clean_title(title)\n    slug = _slug_for(conn, kind, title, slug)\n    now = utc_now()\n    cur = conn.execute(\n        \"INSERT INTO posts (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id, created_at, \"\n        \"updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n        (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id, now, now))\n    conn.commit()\n    return cur.lastrowid\n\n\ndef update_post(conn: sqlite3.Connection, post: sqlite3.Row, *, title: str,\n                slug: str, body_md: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Kind and Author never change. The Slug is locked once first published.\"\"\"\n    title = _clean_title(title)\n    if post[\"first_published_at\"]:\n        slug = post[\"slug\"]\n    else:\n        slug = _slug_for(conn, post[\"kind\"], title, slug or post[\"slug\"], post[\"id\"])\n    conn.execute(\"UPDATE posts SET title = ?, slug = ?, body_md = ?, updated_at = ? \"\n                 \"WHERE id = ?\", (title, slug, body_md, utc_now(), post[\"id\"]))\n    conn.commit()\n\n\ndef get_post(conn: sqlite3.Connection, post_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    return conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM posts WHERE id = ?\", (post_id,)).fetchone()\n\n\ndef list_posts(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    return conn.execute(\n        \"SELECT posts.*, users.name AS author_name FROM posts \"\n        \"JOIN users ON users.id = posts.author_id \"\n        \"ORDER BY posts.updated_at DESC, posts.id DESC\").fetchall()\n\n\ndef publish_post(conn: sqlite3.Connection, post: sqlite3.Row) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Mark as Published. The first-published time is set once and never cleared.\"\"\"\n    now = utc_now()\n    conn.execute(\"UPDATE posts SET status = 'published', updated_at = ?, \"\n                 \"first_published_at = coalesce(first_published_at, ?) WHERE id = ?\",\n                 (now, now, post[\"id\"]))\n    conn.commit()\n\n\ndef unpublish_post(conn: sqlite3.Connection, post: sqlite3.Row) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Back to Draft. first_published_at stays, so the Slug stays locked.\"\"\"\n    conn.execute(\"UPDATE posts SET status = 'draft', updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n                 (utc_now(), post[\"id\"]))\n    conn.commit()\n\n\ndef published_posts(conn: sqlite3.Connection, kind: str | None = None,\n                    limit: int | None = None) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    \"\"\"Published Posts, newest first. Selects no Author: the public site has none.\"\"\"\n    sql = (\"SELECT id, kind, title, slug, body_md, first_published_at FROM posts \"\n           \"WHERE status = 'published'\")\n    args: list = []\n    if kind:\n        sql += \" AND kind = ?\"\n        args.append(kind)\n    sql += \" ORDER BY first_published_at DESC, id DESC\"\n    if limit:\n        sql += \" LIMIT ?\"\n        args.append(limit)\n    return conn.execute(sql, args).fetchall()\n\"\"\"Time: stored in UTC, shown in America/Lima.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom datetime import date, datetime, timezone\nfrom zoneinfo import ZoneInfo\n\nLIMA = ZoneInfo(\"America/Lima\")\n\n\ndef utc_now() -> str:\n    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()\n\n\ndef lima(iso: str | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A stored UTC timestamp as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' in Lima time.\"\"\"\n    if not iso:\n        return \"\"\n    return datetime.fromisoformat(iso).astimezone(LIMA).strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M\")\n\n\nMONTHS_ES = (\"enero\", \"febrero\", \"marzo\", \"abril\", \"mayo\", \"junio\", \"julio\",\n             \"agosto\", \"septiembre\", \"octubre\", \"noviembre\", \"diciembre\")\n\n\ndef today_lima() -> date:\n    return datetime.now(LIMA).date()\n\n\ndef fecha(iso: str | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A stored UTC timestamp as a Lima-time Spanish date: '29 de septiembre de 2026'.\"\"\"\n    if not iso:\n        return \"\"\n    d = datetime.fromisoformat(iso).astimezone(LIMA)\n    return f\"{d.day} de {MONTHS_ES[d.month - 1]} de {d.year}\"\n\"\"\"Post list, editor and Preview. Editors and Admins can do all of it.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Form, HTTPException, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app import auth, content\nfrom app.markdown import render_markdown\nfrom app.web import templates\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/posts\")\n\nKIND_LABELS = {\"news\": \"News\", \"event\": \"Event\", \"menu\": \"Menu\"}\nKIND_LABELS_ES = {\"news\": \"Noticia\", \"event\": \"Evento\", \"menu\": \"Menú de la semana\"}\n\n\ndef form_page(request: Request, user: sqlite3.Row, post: dict, *,\n              error: str | None = None, status_code: int = 200):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/post_form.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Edit post\" if post.get(\"id\") else \"New post\", \"user\": user,\n         \"post\": post, \"error\": error,\n         \"kind_labels\": KIND_LABELS},\n        status_code=status_code)\n\n\ndef load(conn: sqlite3.Connection, post_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    post = content.get_post(conn, post_id)\n    if post is None:\n        raise HTTPException(404, \"Post not found\")\n    return post\n\n\n@router.get(\"\")\ndef post_list(request: Request, user: sqlite3.Row = Depends(auth.current_user),\n              conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(auth.get_db)):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/post_list.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Posts\", \"user\": user, \"posts\": content.list_posts(conn),\n         \"kind_labels\": KIND_LABELS})\n\n\n@router.get(\"/new\")\ndef new_post(request: Request, user: sqlite3.Row = Depends(auth.current_user)):\n    return form_page(request, user, {\"kind\": \"news\", \"title\": \"\", \"slug\": \"\",\n                                     \"body_md\": \"\"})\n\n\n@router.post(\"\")\ndef create_post(request: Request, kind: str = Form(\"\"), title: str = Form(\"\"),\n                slug: str = Form(\"\"), body_md: str = Form(\"\"),\n                user: sqlite3.Row = Depends(auth.current_user),\n                conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(auth.get_db)):\n    try:\n        post_id = content.create_post(conn, kind=kind, title=title, slug=slug,\n                                      body_md=body_md, author_id=user[\"id\"])\n    except content.PostError as exc:\n        return form_page(request, user, {\"kind\": kind, \"title\": title,\n                                         \"slug\": slug, \"body_md\": body_md},\n                         error=str(exc), status_code=422)\n    return RedirectResponse(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{post_id}\")\ndef edit_post(request: Request, post_id: int,\n              user: sqlite3.Row = Depends(auth.current_user),\n              conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(auth.get_db)):\n    return form_page(request, user, dict(load(conn, post_id)))\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{post_id}\")\ndef save_post(request: Request, post_id: int, title: str = Form(\"\"),\n              slug: str = Form(\"\"), body_md: str = Form(\"\"),\n              user: sqlite3.Row = Depends(auth.current_user),\n              conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(auth.get_db)):\n    post = load(conn, post_id)\n    try:\n        content.update_post(conn, post, title=title, slug=slug, body_md=body_md)\n    except content.PostError as exc:\n        return form_page(request, user, {**dict(post), \"title\": title,\n                                         \"slug\": slug, \"body_md\": body_md},\n                         error=str(exc), status_code=422)\n    return RedirectResponse(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{post_id}/publish\")\ndef publish_post(post_id: int, conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(auth.get_db)):\n    content.publish_post(conn, load(conn, post_id))\n    return RedirectResponse(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{post_id}/unpublish\")\ndef unpublish_post(post_id: int, conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(auth.get_db)):\n    content.unpublish_post(conn, load(conn, post_id))\n    return RedirectResponse(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{post_id}/preview\")\ndef preview(request: Request, post_id: int,\n            conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(auth.get_db)):\n    post = load(conn, post_id)\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"public/post.html\",\n        {\"title\": post[\"title\"], \"lang\": \"es\", \"css_path\": \"/style.css\",\n         \"home_path\": \"/\", \"post\": post, \"date_label\": None,\n         \"kind_label\": {"parentUuid":"00c3976b-4200-4778-9c84-6bd9e73ad8a2","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"3b1b5486-f053-4d71-89ab-a4ab94d907fa","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/gianlucabocanegra/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review the working-tree changes since HEAD (app/settings.py .env loader, tests/test_settings.py, .env.example) for ticket #4 (T03). That is a helper below the two seams, not observable behaviour. This is a soft violation. Check it was intended.\n  \n  (b) Smells\n  - Duplicated Code (main one): `app/settings.py` `load_dotenv` and `scripts/seed_demo.py:22-30` are two copies. The seed's version does not strip quotes, so they already disagree. `scripts/seed_demo.py:34` also repeats `Path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_ENV_FILE\", ROOT/\".env\"))`. Since settings now loads .env at import, the seed's own loader is redundant. Delete it and rely on `settings`. That also removes the behaviour split (Shotgun Surgery risk).\n  - Mysterious Name (minor): `line`, `value` are reassigned/shadowed. `.strip(\"\\\"'\")` is cryptic.\n  - Speculative Generality: none.\n  \n  Bugs and risks in the loader\n  1. Quote handling: `.strip(\"\\\"'\")` strips any leading or trailing quote characters independently. `KEY=\"a'` becomes `a`, and `KEY=it's` keeps its apostrophe only by luck (`it's'` would lose the trailing one). Mismatched quotes are stripped. A value with a legitimate edge quote, such as `\"'quoted'\"`, is over-stripped. Inline comments (`KEY=v # c`) are kept in the value. `export KEY=v` yields the key `export KEY`. Fix: strip only when the first and last characters match.\n  2. Import-time side effect: it mutates `os.environ` and reads a file on `import app.settings`. Constants such as `SECRET_KEY` are then fixed at import. The pattern is acceptable, but it makes test isolation hard.\n  3. Test isolation: `test_dotenv_fills_missing_variables_only` mutates the real `os.environ` via `setdefault`. The `monkeypatch.delenv` calls at the end do not undo that: the keys were set by the loader, not by monkeypatch, so they only clean up because delenv was called earlier with raising=False. `CMS_SITE_TITLE` is set to the Golf title and is removed manually at the end. This is fragile: if an assertion fails, the cleanup is skipped and the variables leak into later tests. Use `monkeypatch.setattr(os, \"environ\", dict(os.environ))`, or `monkeypatch.setenv` first so monkeypatch restores it. Also, `import os` sits mid-function.\n  4. Real `.env` leak into tests: importing `app.settings` reads the developer's real `.env` unless `CMS_ENV_FILE` is set. `run_seed` sets `CMS_ENV_FILE` to a nonexistent file, which is good. But the in-process tests (conftest, TestClient) import settings without it, so a local `.env` (CMS_DATABASE, SECRET_KEY, CMS_BASE_PATH) can change test behaviour. Consider setting `CMS_ENV_FILE` in conftest before the import.\n  5. `path.read_text()` has no explicit encoding, so it uses the locale default. A UTF-8 file with accents, like the test's \"entre comillas\", could break on a non-UTF-8 locale. Use `encoding=\"utf-8\"`.\n  6. The empty-value line `KEY=` sets an empty string via `setdefault`. That is fine, but it blocks the code default because `os.environ.get` returns \"\" rather than the fallback.\n</agent-message>"}

Test added. |\n| `read_text()` used the locale encoding | **Fixed.** `encoding=\"utf-8\"`, with an accented value in the test. |\n| The in-process tests could read a developer's real `.env` | **Fixed.** `tests/conftest.py` sets `CMS_ENV_FILE` to `os.devnull` before importing `app`. |\n| Test mutated the real `os.environ` and cleaned up by hand | **Fixed.** Tests swap `os.environ` for a dict via `monkeypatch`, so nothing leaks even if an assertion fails. `import os` moved to the top. |\n| `tests/test_settings.py` calls the `load_dotenv` helper directly (below the two seams in spec #1) | **Kept.** A subprocess test would only re-prove the same parsing. The seed test in `test_t01_login.py` already covers the real `CMS_ENV_FILE` path end to end. |\n| Loader runs at import (side effect on `os.environ`) | **Kept.** `SECRET_KEY`, `SITE_TITLE` and the other constants need it before they are read. Real environment variables still win. |\n| Inline comments (`KEY=v # c`), `export KEY=v` and empty values are not handled | **Kept.** `.env.example` uses none of them. Not worth a parser for this project. |\n\n### Spec\n- \"The site title comes from `CMS_SITE_TITLE`, set to the club's name in `.env.example`\": **met.** `.env.example` and the local `.env` now say \"Golf & Country Club of Trujillo\", and `settings` now loads `.env`, so `cms publish` and `cms serve` use it. (The spec reviewer could not see the ticket body and did not read `settings.py`, so it could not confirm this itself.)\n- Scope creep flagged: the loader itself and the `CMS_ENV_FILE` override. **Kept.** Without them the title never reaches the site unless exported by hand. The override is what keeps the seed test and the suite isolated from a real `.env`.\n- Still open, as before: `cms deploy` and the README Live URL.\n\nSuite: 81 passed.\nEOF\ngh issue comment 4 --body-file /tmp/claude-1000/-home-gianlucabocanegra-iphs400-mp2-cms/2969bd27-5c03-4262-befb-faf837eaf329/scratchpad/review2.md","description":"Post second review findings on issue 4"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3964,"cache_read_input_tokens":87295,"output_tokens":1315,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":88},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3964,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1315,"cache_read_input_tokens":87295,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3964,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3964},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01NNJt4kRo6oisELwm1Xs57E":{"command":"cat > /tmp/claude-1000/-home-gianlucabocanegra-iphs400-mp2-cms/2969bd27-5c03-4262-befb-faf837eaf329/scratchpad/review2.md <<'EOF'\n## /code-review of T03, second pass (`.env` loader and club title; fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app import accounts\nfrom app.main import create_app\nfrom tests.conftest import DEMO_USERS, csrf_from\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nADMIN = DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"]\n\n\ndef sign_in(client, email, password):\n    token = csrf_from(client.get(\"/login\"))\n    return client.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": email, \"password\": password,\n                                       \"csrf_token\": token},\n                       follow_redirects=False)\n\n\ndef test_login_redirects_into_the_console(client):\n    response = sign_in(client, ADMIN[\"email\"], ADMIN[\"password\"])\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert client.get(\"/admin\").status_code == 200\n\n\ndef test_email_is_case_insensitive(client):\n    response = sign_in(client, ADMIN[\"email\"].upper(), ADMIN[\"password\"])\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n\n\ndef test_wrong_email_and_wrong_password_look_identical(client):\n    unknown = sign_in(client, \"nobody@example.test\", \"whatever\")\n    wrong_pw = sign_in(client, ADMIN[\"email\"], \"not-the-password\")\n    assert unknown.status_code == wrong_pw.status_code == 401\n    for response in (unknown, wrong_pw):\n        assert \"wrong email or password\" in response.text.lower()\n    assert \"wrong email or password\" not in client.get(\"/login\").text.lower()\n\n\ndef test_password_never_appears_in_response_or_logs(client, caplog):\n    caplog.set_level(\"DEBUG\")\n    bad = \"hunter2-very-secret\"\n    response = sign_in(client, ADMIN[\"email\"], bad)\n    assert bad not in response.text\n    assert bad not in caplog.text\n    ok = sign_in(client, ADMIN[\"email\"], ADMIN[\"password\"])\n    assert ADMIN[\"password\"] not in ok.text\n    assert ADMIN[\"password\"] not in caplog.text\n\n\ndef test_passwords_are_stored_as_argon2_hashes(db_path):\n    # The one place a test reads storage: the criterion is about storage itself.\n    rows = sqlite3.connect(db_path).execute(\n        \"SELECT password_hash FROM users\").fetchall()\n    assert rows\n    for (stored,) in rows:\n        assert stored.startswith(\"$argon2\")\n        assert \"test-admin-pw\" not in stored and \"test-editor-pw\" not in stored\n\n\ndef test_logout_ends_the_session(client_as):\n    c = client_as(\"admin\")\n    assert c.get(\"/admin\").status_code == 200\n    token = csrf_from(c.get(\"/admin\"))\n    assert c.post(\"/logout\", data={\"csrf_token\": token},\n                  follow_redirects=False).status_code == 303\n    later = c.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert later.status_code == 303 and later.headers[\"location\"] == \"/login\"\n\n\ndef test_logout_invalidates_a_copied_session_cookie(client_as, db_path):\n    c = client_as(\"admin\")\n    stolen = dict(c.cookies)\n    c.post(\"/logout\", data={\"csrf_token\": csrf_from(c.get(\"/admin\"))})\n    replay = TestClient(create_app(db_path), cookies=stolen)\n    assert replay.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False).status_code == 303\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path\", [\"/admin\", \"/admin/pages\", \"/admin/users\",\n                                  \"/admin/anything-else\"])\ndef test_signed_out_visitor_is_sent_to_login(client, path):\n    response = client.get(path, follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/login\"\n\n\ndef test_deactivated_user_cannot_sign_in(client, db_path):\n    accounts.set_active(db_path, DEMO_USERS[\"editor\"][\"email\"], False)\n    response = sign_in(client, DEMO_USERS[\"editor\"][\"email\"],\n                       DEMO_USERS[\"editor\"][\"password\"])\n    assert response.status_code == 401\n    assert client.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False).status_code == 303\n\n\ndef test_user_deactivated_while_signed_in_is_refused_next_request(client_as, db_path):\n    c = client_as(\"editor\")\n    assert c.get(\"/admin\").status_code == 200\n    accounts.set_active(db_path, DEMO_USERS[\"editor\"][\"email\"], False)\n    response = c.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code == 303 and response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/login\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path\", [\"/admin/pages\", \"/admin/users\"])\ndef test_editor_is_refused_from_admin_areas_and_admin_is_not(client_as, path):\n    assert client_as(\"editor\").get(path).status_code == 403\n    assert client_as(\"admin\").get(path).status_code == 200\n\n\ndef test_editor_can_reach_the_dashboard(client_as):\n    assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin\").status_code == 200\n\n\ndef test_editor_does_not_see_admin_navigation(client_as):\n    html = client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin\").text\n    assert \"/admin/users\" not in html and \"/admin/pages\" not in html\n\n\ndef test_login_without_a_valid_csrf_token_is_rejected(client):\n    creds = {\"email\": ADMIN[\"email\"], \"password\": ADMIN[\"password\"]}\n    assert client.post(\"/login\", data=creds).status_code == 403\n    client.get(\"/login\")\n    assert client.post(\"/login\", data={**creds, \"csrf_token\": \"forged\"}\n                       ).status_code == 403\n    assert client.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False).status_code == 303\n\n\ndef test_logout_without_a_valid_csrf_token_is_rejected(client_as):\n    c = client_as(\"admin\")\n    assert c.post(\"/logout\").status_code == 403\n    assert c.post(\"/logout\", data={\"csrf_token\": \"forged\"}).status_code == 403\n    assert c.get(\"/admin\").status_code == 200  # still signed in\n\n\ndef test_a_token_from_another_session_is_rejected(client_as, db_path):\n    other = TestClient(create_app(db_path))\n    foreign = csrf_from(other.get(\"/login\"))\n    c = client_as(\"admin\")\n    assert c.post(\"/logout\", data={\"csrf_token\": foreign}).status_code == 403\n\n\ndef test_each_app_gets_its_own_database(tmp_path):\n    a, b = tmp_path / \"a.db\", tmp_path / \"b.db\"\n    accounts.seed_users(a, admin_password=\"pw-a\", editor_password=\"pw-e\")\n    ca, cb = TestClient(create_app(a)), TestClient(create_app(b))\n    assert sign_in(ca, ADMIN[\"email\"], \"pw-a\").status_code == 303\n    assert sign_in(cb, ADMIN[\"email\"], \"pw-a\").status_code == 401\n\n\ndef run_seed(tmp_path, **env):\n    clean = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items()\n             if k not in (\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\", \"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")}\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [sys.executable, str(ROOT / \"scripts\" / \"seed_demo.py\")],\n        env={**clean, \"CMS_DATABASE\": str(tmp_path / \"seeded.db\"),\n             \"CMS_ENV_FILE\": str(tmp_path / \"no.env\"), **env},\n        capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=ROOT)\n\n\ndef test_seed_refuses_without_passwords(tmp_path):\n    result = run_seed(tmp_path)\n    assert result.returncode != 0\n    assert not (tmp_path / \"seeded.db\").exists()\n\n\ndef test_seed_creates_admin_and_editor_from_environment(tmp_path):\n    result = run_seed(tmp_path, CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=\"seed-admin-pw\",\n                      CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD=\"seed-editor-pw\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr\n    assert \"seed-admin-pw\" not in result.stdout + result.stderr\n    app = create_app(tmp_path / \"seeded.db\")\n    assert sign_in(TestClient(app), ADMIN[\"email\"], \"seed-admin-pw\").status_code == 303\n    assert sign_in(TestClient(app), DEMO_USERS[\"editor\"][\"email\"],\n                   \"seed-editor-pw\").status_code == 303\n    # Running it twice is harmless.\n    again = run_seed(tmp_path, CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=\"seed-admin-pw\",\n                     CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD=\"seed-editor-pw\")\n    assert again.returncode == If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Only continue to apply ongoing behavioral guidelines from these skills where still relevant.\n\n### Skill: code-review\nPath: projectSettings:code-review\n\nBase directory for this skill: /home/gianlucabocanegra/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review the working-tree changes since HEAD (app/settings.py .env loader, tests/test_settings.py, .env.example) for ticket #4 (T03).
